nodes.stepInstructions:
Do NOT write code. Produce the plan the other steps will follow.

1. Read .agentsroom/memory/INDEX.md (local mirror, no tool call) and any note that matches the task, BEFORE exploring the codebase.
2. Open _docs/adr/README.md and match the task against its Area column. If a governing ADR exists, follow it and cite it by number. If the change is architectural and NO ADR covers it, say so explicitly in risks — do not invent an architecture.
3. Locate the code with codebase-memory-mcp (search_graph, trace_path, get_code_snippet) BEFORE reaching for grep.
4. Identify which submodule owns the change and read its own .github/copilot-instructions.md — it is authoritative and overrides the root one.
5. Post the plan with team_post_note: files to touch, the service/slice that owns each, edge cases, and the concrete steps QA should use to verify. Summarise it in featureSummary.

This is a HIGH-STAKES ticket (security / tenant-isolation / auth / migration / money). Be exhaustive about edge cases and explicitly flag any assumption you cannot verify.

Before reusing or reimplementing anything, check whether it already exists in this repo — especially under _tools/ (asma-cli already owns Jira, Confluence, Bitbucket and GitHub integrations). Reimplementing an existing tool in a second language is a defect, not a design choice.

Every rung a DIFFERENT vendor. Fallback rungs must CROSS VENDORS — two models from the same vendor usually share one usage allowance, so a same-vendor fallback protects nothing. If you are running below rung 2, say so in your handoff.

If the request is ambiguous, use team_ask rather than guessing.
